full_judgment:
4. Mr Mustafizur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioners referring section 28 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain ("Ain") 2003 submits that section 28(3) of the Ain. provides that in the event-of dismissal or disposal of the first Artha Rin Execution Case the Decree Holder may file further Execution Case within one year from the date of dismissal of the first Execution Case and any Execution Case filed beyond one year after dismissal or disposal of the first execution case shall be barred by limitation and the Adalat shall reject the same directly without accepting the said case. He further submits that from the statements made in the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act filed before the Artha Rin Adalat by the Decree Holder Bank seeking condonation of delay in filing the second Execution Case, it will show that the jari Case was not filed within the period prescribed by law but admittedly it was filed after a lapse of more than two years. So, as per section 28(3) of the Ain, the instant Artha Jan Case is hopelessly barred by limitation and as such, the continuation of such proceeding is palpably illegal and an abuse of the process of the Court. 

 9. It appears from the application in Artha Jari Case No. 283 of 2011 that the said execution case was filed on 30-11-2011, Admittedly first Artha Jari Case No. 242 of 2005 was dismissed for default on 9-4-2009. The Decree Holder Bank as per aforesaid provision of law ought to have filed the second Execution Case within one year from the date of dismissal of earlier Execution Case, but the instant execution case was filed beyond two years the dismissal of the earlier Execution Case. Moreover, it appears from the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act (Annexure-C) that the 1st Execution Case No. 242 of 2005 was filed on 17-7-2005 and 2nd Execution Case has been filed on 30-11-2011 i.e. after six years from the date of filing of the 1st Execution Case. As such the instant Jari Case has become barred by limitation not only under section 28 (3) but also under section 28(4) of the Ain. 

 10. The provisions of section 5 of the Limitation Act is not applicable to the proceedings pending before any Tribunals because mostly the Tribunals shall be constituted only by an act of special laws which prescribe all mode of remedies and it never borrows any provisions from outside sources and to put in other words such Special Laws can be called as "Self-contained Enactments." 

 11. Likewise for the enforcement of the Decree and, Orders passed by the Court of law the litigants has to file an Execution petition before the Executing Court by exercising the provisions as enshrined under section 28 of the Ain with the aid of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure. For filing such an Execution Case section 5 of the Limitation Act is strictly not applicable because the Execution Petition should be filed within the time period originally fixed under the Act failing which the Decree Holder in the eyes of law had exhausted his lawful remedies, as such, it cannot thereafter, enforce its rights as enshrined under the Decree, Order, etc. passed by the Court in its favour.
